architecture.batch_norm_note: BatchNorm1d is present in the upstream source but was omitted from the repository's earlier architecture summary in docs/research_definition.md 5.9.
architecture.decoder_block: Linear -> BatchNorm1d -> ReLU for each of [2048, 2048, 2048] in reverse, then Linear(2048, 5836) with no BatchNorm and no activation
architecture.encoder_block: Linear -> BatchNorm1d -> ReLU for each of [2048, 2048, 2048], then Linear(2048, 16) with no BatchNorm and no activation

brushless_motor_limitation.permitted: published/reproduced benchmark discrimination on the released BrushlessMotor cohort

dataset.version_note: Zenodo API version field is null; no version number is asserted.

preprocessing.length_handling: zero-pad if short, truncate if long, to int(fs * 0.1)
preprocessing.normalisation: std_window (per window, per channel, epsilon in denominator)
preprocessing.normalisation_fitting: none - applied independently to train, validation and test

published_reference_values.source: Albertini et al., DCASE 2024 Workshop, paper Table 4 (authors' own results)
published_reference_values.usage_rule: may be compared against, never optimised towards

purpose: Faithful reproduction of the published IMAD-DS official baseline, as a historical comparability anchor. This is not the MechaSight deployment protocol; Protocol B remains the primary leakage-controlled benchmark.

reproduction_tolerance.justification: Upstream seeds torch and the sklearn split but does not disable cuDNN nondeterminism, and its early stopping (patience 3) means a single epoch's difference changes the final weights. Run-to-run variation of a fraction of an AUC point is therefore expected even from the authors' own code, so bitwise equality is not a reasonable criterion. 0.5 points is adopted as the near-exact band and 2.0 points as the material-deviation boundary. Both were fixed before any MechaSight Protocol-A test score was computed.

robotic_arm_overlap_disclosure.permitted_language: recording overlap creates a credible mechanism for optimistic bias; the magnitude is to be measured
robotic_arm_overlap_disclosure.reason: Protocol A exists to reproduce the released evaluation; making it parent-disjoint would defeat its purpose.

scope_limits.reason: Protocol A and Protocol B differ in split, preprocessing, model family and representation simultaneously, so their difference does not isolate the effect of parent-recording overlap. A controlled experiment holding model and preprocessing constant while varying only the grouping is required, and is not performed here.

scoring.anomaly_score: per-window reconstruction MSE over the concatenated multi-sensor vector

auc.rule: pair scores 1 only when normal_score < anomaly_score; exact ties score zero

scoring.per_sensor_columns: f_<sensor> from the joint reconstruction; s_<sensor> from masked-input evaluation
scoring.segment_aggregation: median of the segment's window scores

split.note: Regime T: the released target-normal training segments are included in training, as upstream does.

training.checkpoint_selection: upstream stores best_model_state = self.state_dict(), which holds live tensor references rather than a copy, so the restored weights are the final epoch's, not the best-validation epoch's. Reproduced, not corrected.
training.determinism: upstream does not set cudnn.deterministic or use_deterministic_algorithms, so GPU training is seeded but not bitwise reproducible. Faithful reproduction preserves this; an optional deterministic mode is NOT used.
training.device: environment parameter; upstream comments explicitly instruct adapting it per machine ('mps', 'cuda', or 'cpu')
training.early_stopping: stop when validation loss has not improved for 3 consecutive epochs
training.loss: utilities.MSE = mean squared error over dim=1, then mean over the batch
training.seed_scope: torch.manual_seed and torch.cuda.manual_seed; sklearn train_test_split random_state

upstream.license: No LICENSE file exists in the pinned upstream tree. Upstream source is therefore NOT vendored into this repository; only its verified identity and behaviour are recorded, and the reproduction is independently implemented.
upstream.verification: Re-fetched at the pinned commit and verified byte-for-byte against the GitHub tree: all four git blob SHA-1 values match. The Phase-2 recorded SHA-256 values are reproduced exactly by the CRLF-converted form of the same bytes, so the Phase-2 provenance hashes were computed after Windows line-ending conversion. Content is identical; only the recorded hash form was non-portable.
